title: How to avoid the "connect wallet to verify" airdrop scam (2026 update)
excerpt: Pasting a public address to check airdrop eligibility is safe. Signing a transaction to 'verify' your wallet is how almost every airdrop draining attack of 2024-2026 started. Here's exactly what to watch for.
body_md:
## Why this matters

The single biggest financial risk in the airdrop space is not picking the wrong project — it's getting drained by a fake checker site. Throughout 2024, 2025, and into 2026, the dominant attack pattern has stayed identical: lure users to a fake "airdrop checker" or "claim portal" with a Google Ad or Twitter reply, ask them to "connect wallet to verify eligibility," then drain everything in the wallet via a hidden malicious signature.

The attack is so durable because the user-facing prompt looks identical to a legitimate dapp interaction. If you understand exactly what is happening under the hood, the warning signs become obvious.

## What "connect wallet" actually does

Connecting a wallet to a site does NOT, on its own, give the site any power to move your funds. Connection only shares your public address. The site needs you to *sign* something to do anything malicious.

The danger is in the very next prompt that almost always follows. The site will request one of these signature types:

- `permit` or `permit2` — gives the site permission to spend a specific token without a separate approval transaction. One signature, your stablecoins are gone.
- `setApprovalForAll` — gives blanket NFT spend rights. Your Bored Ape is gone in the next block.
- A swap or transfer transaction that has been crafted to drain a specific token.

Legitimate airdrop checkers DO NOT need any of these signatures. Pasting a public address is enough to query the blockchain.

## The cardinal rule

> If a site asks you to sign anything to *check* eligibility, close the tab.

The only signature that should appear during a real airdrop flow is the actual **claim transaction**, after the snapshot, on the project's official URL. And even then, simulate it in a wallet that supports transaction simulation (Rabby, Frame, OneKey) before approving.

## How to verify a checker is safe

1. **URL check.** Type the official URL by hand. Never click a link from a reply, DM, or sponsored search result. Bookmark legit sites the first time you visit.
2. **No connection prompt.** A safe checker has a text input for an address. That's it. No "Connect Wallet" button on the checker page.
3. **Read-only confirmation.** The checker explicitly states it does not request signatures. (Ours does — see the [/check page](/check).)
4. **No urgency.** Real airdrops do not have "claim in the next 5 minutes or lose forever" timers. Anything that pressures speed is a phish.

## Wallet hygiene if you farm airdrops

- Use a **fresh wallet** with no other funds for any interaction with a new dapp.
- After confirming a dapp is safe, you can graduate it to your "farming" wallet with small balances.
- **Never** sign anything from your main wallet that holds long-term assets.
- Use a **hardware wallet** for the main vault. The cost is $80; the upside is a drainer can't pull funds without physical confirmation.
- Revoke approvals quarterly via [revoke.cash](https://revoke.cash).

## What to do if you've already signed something suspicious

1. Move every asset out of the affected wallet immediately to a fresh wallet — gas willing.
2. Revoke all approvals on revoke.cash (this may not save you if a `permit` was already used to transfer).
3. Report the phish on Twitter / Telegram so others avoid it.
4. Assume the wallet is permanently compromised. Never use it again, even after revoking.

## Bottom line

Paste, don't sign. Every credible airdrop checker — including this one — works on public addresses alone. Treat any prompt for a signature during eligibility verification as definitive proof you're on a phishing site, and close the tab.

title: How to qualify for L2 airdrops in 2026 (without sybil flagging)
excerpt: A practical playbook for farming L2 airdrops that survive the inevitable sybil filter. Diversity beats volume; consistency beats burst farming; and unique behavioral signatures beat bot-perfect activity.
body_md:
## What changed in 2026

The ZK-rollup wave of 2024-2025 (zkSync, Starknet, Linea, Scroll) trained teams how to filter sybils aggressively. Every major L2 airdrop since LayerZero has applied multi-axis sybil detection: address-graph clustering, behavioral fingerprinting, fund-source analysis, and timing distribution. Pre-2024 farming techniques (50-wallet stamping, identical-amount transactions, same-day funding) are now reliably filtered out.

The modern L2 airdrop is best understood as **a behavioral pattern recognition contest, not a volume contest**. You are trying to look like a real user who happens to use multiple wallets, not a farmer.

## The signals that matter

From every published sybil-detection methodology (Hop Protocol's, LayerZero's, Optimism's), these are the axes graders use:

1. **Funding source diversity.** Wallets funded from the same CEX address within the same hour are clustered. Use different CEXes, different times, different amounts. Better: peer-to-peer funding from a fresh wallet you control, mixed with CEX withdrawals.
2. **Time distribution.** Real users don't transact in 5-minute bursts on 30 wallets. Spread activity across days and weeks, with natural gaps.
3. **Dapp diversity.** Touching only the bridge marks you as a farmer. Real users swap, lend, mint NFTs, vote, and bridge.
4. **Transaction value variance.** All your txs being $10 ± $1 is a red flag. Real value distributions are skewed and noisy.
5. **Gas pattern.** Submitting only at minimum priority fee marks you. Sometimes overpay; sometimes wait.
6. **Holding behavior.** Bridge → swap → bridge back same day = farmer. Bridge → keep position for weeks = user.

## The minimum viable strategy

For any active L2 with a likely retroactive drop:

- **30+ days** between first activity and snapshot. Anything shorter is increasingly filtered.
- **3+ unique dapps** touched: bridge + DEX + lending or NFT.
- **5-15 transactions/month** across those dapps. Quality over quantity.
- **Maintain a non-trivial position** (e.g., $50+ LP, $100+ lent) across the snapshot.
- **Do something native to the chain** — a Linea-only protocol, a Base-only mint, a Scroll-only social app. Generic protocols deployed everywhere are deprioritized.

## Wallet count tradeoff

1 wallet that looks like a real user beats 20 wallets that look like farmers. If you must run multiples:

- Maximum 3-5 wallets across an L2.
- Each wallet funded from a different source.
- Each wallet's behavioral profile materially different (one heavy DEX, one heavy lending, one heavy NFT).
- No common withdrawal address pre-snapshot.

More than 5 wallets per L2 is a losing strategy in 2026.

## Chains worth farming right now

At time of writing (May 2026):

- **Monad** — testnet active, no token, $244M raised, very likely retroactive.
- **MegaETH** — testnet active, team has confirmed activity will be counted.
- **Linea** — LXP/LXP-L points active, ConsenSys has not committed to a token but the system is designed like a pre-TGE accumulation.
- **Berachain** — mainnet live, BGT boost emissions are paying out weekly.
- **Sonic** — Season 2 points open through September 2026 snapshot.

See the [/check page](/check) to test whether any wallets you've already used would qualify for finalized snapshots.

## What kills your allocation

- **Funding from a sanctioned mixer.** Allocation goes to zero. Use clean funds.
- **Behavioral clustering with known farms.** If your wallet's behavior matches a published sybil cluster, you're cut.
- **Trading exclusively with yourself.** Wash trades across your own wallets are detected by every modern grader.
- **Activity ending exactly at snapshot.** A natural user keeps using the chain after the airdrop too. Many graders include a post-snapshot continuation check.

## Bottom line

Farming L2 airdrops profitably in 2026 means looking like a real user who has multiple wallets, not a farmer trying to look like a real user. The fewer wallets, the more diverse the behavior, the longer the timeline, the higher the expected value per wallet.

title: What is a retroactive airdrop? (And why they're the highest-EV category)
excerpt: A retroactive airdrop rewards on-chain activity that already happened before the token was announced. They consistently produce the largest per-wallet payouts — but only for users who happened to use the protocol naturally, which is the catch.
body_md:
## Definition

A retroactive airdrop distributes tokens to wallets that interacted with a protocol *before* the token was announced. The protocol team takes an on-chain snapshot of historical users, applies a scoring formula, and allocates tokens proportionally.

Key distinction from other airdrop types:

- **Retroactive** rewards past activity. You qualify by accident, by being an early user. Examples: Uniswap (UNI, 2020), 1inch, dYdX V2, ENS, Arbitrum (ARB), Optimism (OP), LayerZero (ZRO), Wormhole (W), Jupiter (JUP).
- **Points / live programs** reward present activity. You qualify by participating in a known points system. Examples: EigenLayer points, Ether.fi loyalty, Pendle YT.
- **Testnet** rewards activity on a chain's testnet pre-mainnet. Examples: Aptos, Sui, ZK-Sync (partially), Monad (upcoming).
- **Task-based** rewards completing a defined quest, usually via Galxe or Zealy.

## Why retroactive drops have the highest historical EV

Three reasons:

1. **Smaller eligible population.** Pre-announcement users are by definition early adopters. The denominator on token-per-wallet is small.
2. **Strong product-market fit signal.** Protocols willing to distribute retroactively typically have real users and revenue — these aren't vapor coins. The token retains value better.
3. **Lower farming risk.** You can't farm what hasn't been announced. The early users qualified through genuine usage, not deliberate gaming, which limits sybil dilution.

**The catch:** by definition, you can't *target* a future retroactive drop, because they're not announced. The best you can do is interact with high-quality protocols that *might* tokenize, betting that some of them will reward early activity.

## The retroactive-drop heuristic

Protocols that are most likely to do a retroactive drop tend to:

- Have raised $20M+ from top-tier VCs (Paradigm, a16z, Coinbase Ventures, Polychain).
- Have a tokenless competitor that already tokenized (creates pressure).
- Be deployed for 12+ months with measurable user growth and TVL.
- Have a public Discord with talk of "community ownership" but no token announcement.
- Be on an L2 or L1 that itself rewarded retroactively (Arbitrum, Optimism, Base ecosystem protocols).

DefiLlama's [airdrops page](https://defillama.com/airdrops) tracks the universe of tokenless protocols — a useful candidate list. We pull from this source for our [home page](/) listings.

## How retroactive scoring usually works

The exact formula is always different, but common ingredients:

- **Time-weighted volume.** Activity that happened earlier in the protocol's life weighs more.
- **Diversity bonus.** Using multiple features of the protocol scores higher than only using one.
- **Withholding penalty.** Wallets that bridged everything out shortly after each use are scored down.
- **Sybil filter.** Wallets in known farming clusters are excluded or capped.
- **NFT or governance participation.** Voting on proposals or holding the protocol's NFTs often gets a multiplier.

## Examples worth studying

- **Uniswap UNI (Sep 2020)**: 400 UNI to every wallet that had ever used Uniswap. ~$1,200 at distribution, $5K+ at peak. Pure flat-rate retroactive.
- **ENS (Nov 2021)**: Allocation based on time-weighted name ownership. Subdomains counted. Most generous retroactive of the cycle.
- **LayerZero ZRO (Jun 2024)**: Heavy sybil filtering — about 60% of wallets that were flagged received nothing. Surviving wallets received $300-$30K depending on activity diversity.
- **Wormhole W (Apr 2024)**: Cross-chain bridge volume weighted, with bonus for early Solana → EVM users.
- **Jupiter JUP (Jan 2024)**: Solana DEX, distributed to wallets that had >$1k cumulative trading volume. Median allocation around $1,200.

## Strategy: maximize exposure, minimize farming

If retroactive drops are the highest-EV category, the rational approach is to *be a genuine user* of many high-quality tokenless protocols. Not to farm them. Concretely:

1. Maintain real LP, real lending positions, real NFT holdings across 5-15 protocols you've genuinely chosen for product reasons.
2. Avoid the temptation to script transactions. Real-user behavior is the signal you want.
3. Be patient — retroactive drops typically land 12-36 months after a protocol's launch.
4. Track tokenless protocols via this site or DefiLlama. When one announces a token, check the [/check page](/check) — your wallet may already qualify.

## Bottom line

A retroactive airdrop rewards past usage. They consistently produce the largest payouts and are the hardest to farm. The way to win them is to be a real user of many high-quality protocols — and then let time do the work.

title: Best Bitcoin cashback apps in Europe (2026): Satsback vs Lolli vs Fold
excerpt: Lolli and Fold dominate Bitcoin cashback — in the United States. If you shop from Europe, most of them simply won't let you in. Here's what actually works for EU shoppers, with the honest trade-offs.
body_md:
## The catch nobody mentions: geography

Search "Bitcoin cashback app" and you'll get glowing lists of Lolli, Fold, and the Cash App Bitcoin Boost. They're all legitimate — and almost all of them are **US-only**. If you're shopping from the Netherlands, Germany, or anywhere in the EU, the biggest names either block you at sign-up or support a handful of global brands that don't include the stores you actually buy from.

That single fact decides which app is right for you. So before comparing rates, sort by where you live.

## Availability, honestly

| App | Where it works | Stores | Payout |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lolli** | United States only | 10,000+ (US) | Bitcoin, in-app |
| **Fold** | United States only | Debit-card rewards | Bitcoin / sats |
| **Cash App Boost** | United States only | Square sellers | Bitcoin |
| **Satsback** | Global, strong in **Europe** | European + global brands | Bitcoin via Lightning |

For a US shopper, Lolli's catalogue is unmatched and its referral is generous. For a European shopper, Lolli isn't an option at all — and that's where **Satsback** wins by default, because it actually carries the stores Europeans use: HEMA, MediaMarkt, Thuisbezorgd, Zalando, Booking.com, Lidl, and hundreds more.

## How the two models differ

**Lolli (US)** is a closed rewards app: you shop through its extension, earn Bitcoin, and withdraw once you clear a threshold. Its strength is scale and a $10-per-referral programme.

**Satsback (EU-friendly)** is a Lightning-native cashback layer: you shop through its extension or site, earn a percentage back in **sats paid to a Lightning wallet you control** — no custodial balance to babysit, no KYC. Its strength is European store coverage and self-custody.

Neither is magic. Both rely on affiliate tracking, which means a share of orders don't register the first time.

## The honest downside of all of them

Affiliate cashback — Bitcoin or fiat — is never 100% reliable. Independent users report roughly two in three orders track cleanly. The fixes are the same across every app:

- Turn off ad-blockers on the store's tab.
- Don't stack a second coupon or cashback extension at checkout.
- Make the cashback tab the last thing you touch before you pay.
- If an order doesn't appear in a few days, support can chase it with your receipt.

If you want a guaranteed discount instead of probabilistic cashback, look for the fixed **discount-code** offers (common on Bitcoin-native shops) rather than percentage cashback.

## So which should you use?

- **In the US:** Lolli for catalogue size; Fold if you want a Bitcoin rewards debit card. 
- **In Europe:** Satsback, because the US apps won't serve you and Satsback carries your actual stores. Browse the ones worth using on our [store directory](/shop), or the Dutch cluster at [/nl/shop](/nl/shop).
- **Everywhere:** pair whichever cashback app you use with an exchange sign-up bonus (a one-time top-up of free Bitcoin) — we compare those on the [bonuses page](/bonus).

## Bottom line

The "best" Bitcoin cashback app is mostly decided by your address. Americans are spoiled for choice with Lolli and Fold. Europeans have effectively one strong option — Satsback — and the upside is that it pays in self-custodial sats at the stores you already shop. Just go in knowing the tracking isn't perfect, and treat the sats as a bonus on spending you'd do anyway.
